pathway.title: GENMAB A/S — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Revenue quality is high today but finite, because one product family generates most of it and its patents expire from 2029. Revenue was USD 3,238 million in nine months, up 21.64%, and DARZALEX royalties were USD 2,057 million, or 63.53% of revenue, up 17.95% on the prior year. Johnson & Johnson develops, sells and bears the costs of the product, so Genmab earns the royalty without selling or manufacturing cost, which is why it converts to cash and also why Genmab cannot steer it. US patent rights end in 2029, European rights in 2031 and Japanese rights begin to expire in 2030, and the annual filing expects royalties to fall materially from 2029, so the debt has to be paid down before the royalty base shrinks. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation C1

Leverage is the main financial constraint and cannot be stated on EBITDA, because 2025 depreciation and amortization are not supplied. Total debt of USD 4,992 million is 4.78x last-twelve-months operating profit of USD 1,044 million and net debt of USD 3,132 million is 3.00x; on the company's adjusted operating profit of USD 1,356 million the multiples are 3.68x and 2.31x. Management targets gross leverage below 3x within two years of the December 2025 closing. At the nine-month repayment pace of USD 288 million, debt would be about USD 4,512 million by the end of 2027, which is 3.33x adjusted profit and 4.32x reported profit at today's levels, so the target needs profit growth of 10.91% on the adjusted measure or 44.06% on reported profit, or faster repayment. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C16; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-11-06_genmabinterimreportq32025.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash conversion is uneven, and the nine-month result is flattered by a low tax charge. Operating cash flow was USD 574 million against USD 885 million a year earlier, with only USD 3 million in the first quarter and USD 520 million in the third, because receivables, inventories, contract liabilities and other payables together absorbed USD 354 million. Taxes paid fell to USD 97 million from USD 317 million and the estimated tax rate dropped to 3.4%, which the company says is not indicative of future periods; at 18.9%, the prior-year rate, tax expense would have been USD 111.65 million higher over the nine months. Free cash flow of USD 555 million was 51.97% of EBITDA. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 28, 35; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-07_genmabinterimreportq12026.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Debt service is covered with room to spare today, but part of the room is being used for share purchases. Free cash flow, which is after interest, covered nine-month principal repayments of USD 288 million 1.93x and left USD 171 million once USD 96 million of share purchases were paid, and cash rose to USD 1,860 million. A buy-back that runs alongside repayment while leverage is above the management target is a financial-policy choice, and the restricted-payment limits that govern it sit in debt documents that are not supplied. Basis: calculation C9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 44–45; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Liquidity is adequate for the next year, but the refinancing profile cannot be placed. Cash of USD 1,860 million, all bank deposits, is 5.85x current borrowings of USD 318 million, which are the current portions of the Term A and Term B loans, and the notes have no current portion. A USD 500 million revolving facility was arranged in December 2025, but the borrowings note shows no revolver balance and its availability, maturity and conditions are not stated, and the annual filing also refers to an unsecured three-year revolving facility whose size is not stated. Maturity dates, coupons and covenant levels of the term loans and notes are not supplied; the company states that it complied with the Term A covenants at 30 September 2026. Basis: calculation C10; calculation C22; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 45–46; 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 131

The interest burden is manageable and market access looks open. Nine-month cash interest was USD 236 million, covered 4.53x by EBITDA of USD 1,068 million, and the implied cost of debt is about 6.65% on average borrowings. Four interest rate swaps of USD 406 million each, running to 30 June 2028, fix 62.46% of the term loans at carrying value and leave USD 976 million floating, so a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 9.76 million a year. The June 2026 cut in the Term B margin from 3.00% to 2.00% saves about USD 19 million a year on USD 1,900 million and suggests lenders accepted a lower spread six months after closing. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47

Margins are under pressure from launch preparation, and management's levers are real but costly. Revenue rose 21.64% but operating profit fell to USD 986 million from USD 1,007 million, an operating margin of 30.45% against 37.83%, because adjusted operating expenses rose 27.33% (research and development 24.09%, selling, general and administrative 35.65%) as petosemtamab and Rina-S trials and launch teams were funded, and acquisition and integration charges added USD 87 million. Capital expenditure was only USD 19 million, so flexibility sits in research, selling and administrative spend, and cutting it would weaken the pipeline that has to replace DARZALEX royalties. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C20; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 23–24, 34

Guidance points to a heavy fourth quarter. Maintaining the 2026 range implies fourth-quarter adjusted operating expenses of USD 914 million to USD 1,054 million, 41.27% to 62.91% above USD 647 million in the third quarter, and adjusted operating profit between USD -43 million and USD 277 million against USD 452 million, so fourth-quarter operating cash flow would be expected to fall well below the third quarter's USD 520 million unless working capital reverses. Either the range is conservative or launch-related spending steps up sharply. Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6–7

On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and market position, competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, access to refinancing, liquidity and financial policy are average, business diversification and free cash flow stability are weak, and none is strong. The weakest two follow from the same fact, a profit base that rests on one royalty and converts to cash unevenly. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C10

runs.text: Royalty growth on a cost-free stream is the first support for creditors: royalties rose to USD 2,699 million from USD 2,219 million and are paid on partner sales, so each extra dollar of royalty reaches operating profit without Genmab selling cost, which raises debt service capacity while the patents last. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C1

Interest cover is comfortable: EBITDA of USD 1,068 million covered nine-month cash interest of USD 236 million 4.53x and free cash flow of USD 555 million covered principal repayments 1.93x, so the debt is serviced from operations and not from cash on hand. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C9

Deleveraging has started and market access looks open: net debt fell USD 427 million to USD 3,132 million, USD 288 million of term loan principal was repaid and the Term B margin was cut to 2.00%, which lowers interest cost and signals lender appetite. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

Near-term liquidity is sound: cash of USD 1,860 million is 5.85x current borrowings and no note has a current portion, so scheduled repayment in the next twelve months is small against cash on hand. Basis: calculation C10; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, page 45

Concentration is the dominant weakness: DARZALEX royalties are 63.53% of revenue and J&J is 66.99%, and US patents expire in 2029, so the cash flow that services the debt shrinks on a known date and the debt has to be reduced or refinanced against that decline. Basis: calculation C1; 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11

Leverage is high: total debt is 4.78x last-twelve-months operating profit against a management target of below 3x, so deleveraging has to come from repayment and profit growth together, and the cushion for a royalty shortfall is thin. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C16

Cash flow is volatile: operating cash flow fell to USD 574 million from USD 885 million, with USD 3 million in the first quarter, and part of the nine-month result comes from a 3.4% tax rate that the company says will not recur, so debt service capacity in a weak quarter is lower than the nine-month average implies. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C17

Spending is rising faster than revenue: adjusted operating expenses grew 27.33% against revenue growth of 21.64%, and guidance implies a larger fourth quarter, so margin and cash conversion are exposed to launch timing. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C14

Creditor protections cannot be verified: the debt documents, agency views and the amounts of the AbbVie and Chugai claims are not supplied while share purchases continue, so the strength of covenants, restricted-payment limits and any legal loss cannot be sized. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34

runs.text: On 12 December 2025 Genmab completed the acquisition of Merus N.V. for USD 97.00 per share in cash, a transaction value of about USD 8.0 billion, accounted for as an asset acquisition because substantially all of the value is petosemtamab. The agreement was signed on 29 September 2025 and the tender offer began on 21 October 2025. Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-11-06_genmabinterimreportq32025.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 40, 47; 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, page 125

The acquisition was funded with about USD 5.5 billion of new debt and cash on hand: a USD 1 billion Term Loan A, a USD 2 billion Term Loan B, a USD 500 million revolving credit facility, USD 1.5 billion of senior secured notes and USD 1.0 billion of senior unsecured notes, with Genmab Finance LLC named alongside Genmab A/S in the debt documents. At 30 September 2026 the four drawn instruments carried USD 926 million, USD 1,674 million, USD 1,439 million and USD 953 million, and the Term B margin had been cut from 3.00% to 2.00% in June 2026. Coupons, maturities, guarantors and collateral are not supplied, and management's target is gross leverage below 3x within two years of closing. Basis: 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 180–182; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-11-06_genmabinterimreportq32025.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genmab's creditors rely on a concentrated royalty stream, two thirds of revenue from DARZALEX, whose patents expire from 2029, to service the USD 5.5 billion of debt that financed the Merus acquisition, with no sponsor behind them and no disclosed holder above 5.80%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is conventional for a listed company: a nine-member board with a majority of independent directors, an independent audit and finance committee chair, audited accounts, quarterly reporting, no dividends and no material related-party transactions. Creditor protection therefore comes from the credit agreement and the indentures, whose terms are not supplied, and not from a sponsor; share purchases of USD 96 million in 2026 continued while debt was repaid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is concentrated in one product family and one partner. DARZALEX royalties were USD 2,057 million of USD 3,238 million of nine-month 2026 revenue, or 63.53%, and revenue from J&J was 66.99%; the annual filing states 66% for 2025. The royalty tiers run from 12% to 20% of annual net sales, are reduced for biosimilars and patent expiry, and J&J can terminate on 150 days' notice. Patent rights expire in 2029 in the U.S., 2030 in Japan and 2031 in Europe, and the filing expects royalties to decline materially from 2029, so debt has to be reduced well before then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversification is real but slow. Net product sales rose to USD 410 million from USD 280 million, led by EPKINLY in the U.S. and Japan at USD 381 million, and Kesimpta royalties were USD 408 million, yet royalties still made up 83.35% of nine-month revenue. The 2026 guidance of USD 4,325 million to USD 4,525 million of revenue keeps the mix royalty-led, so new products reduce but do not remove the dependence on DARZALEX within the debt tenor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Merus acquisition changed the creditor profile from net cash to leveraged. Genmab paid USD 97.00 per share, about USD 8.0 billion in cash, closed on 12 December 2025 and funded it with about USD 5.5 billion of new debt plus cash on hand. Management targets gross leverage below 3x within two years of closing. The asset acquired, petosemtamab, is in Phase 3, and acquired in-process research and development of USD 8,237 million sits on the balance sheet at 30 September 2026, so the acquisition adds costs before it adds cash and creditors rely on the royalty business to carry the debt while the asset matures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance gives creditors visibility but no external support. There is no sponsor, the largest disclosed holders are BlackRock and Orbis at 5.80% each, management holds 1.27%, and the board is a majority independent with an independent audit and finance committee chair. The auditor's opinions are unqualified and internal control was effective, but Merus, 59.6% of total assets, was excluded from that assessment. The credit agreement and indentures restrict dividends and other distributions, and no dividends have been paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legal exposure is unquantified and involves a key partner. AbbVie's trade secret case over Rina-S resumed in the district court after its import-exclusion complaint to the trade commission ended in July 2026, and Chugai's three Japanese lawsuits over four patents on EPKINLY remain open; no provision is recorded for either. The amounts are not stated, so the exposure cannot be sized, and AbbVie is also Genmab's partner on epcoritamab, so the dispute touches a relationship that carries net product sales and profit sharing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has been moderate since the acquisition. USD 288 million of term loan principal was repaid in nine months, the buy-back programme took USD 96 million, and acquisition and integration charges were USD 87 million. Whether continued share purchases are consistent with creditor protection depends on the restricted-payment baskets in the credit agreement and indentures, which are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the royalty base is still growing: royalties rose to USD 2,699 million from USD 2,219 million, partner sales of DARZALEX grew 19%, the company has no dividend, no sponsor and no related-party leakage, and three Phase 3 trials read out positively in October 2026, which supports the value of the assets that creditors rely on. A listed company with an independent board and quarterly reporting is also easier to monitor than a sponsor-owned borrower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn more favourable if the credit agreement and indentures show wide covenant headroom, long maturities and tight restricted-payment baskets, and if successful launches of epcoritamab, Rina-S or petosemtamab add royalty-independent cash flow before 2029. It would turn less favourable if DARZALEX royalties erode earlier than the patent dates imply, if the AbbVie or Chugai cases are decided against Genmab, or if share purchases accelerate while leverage stays above the management target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 12 December 2025 Genmab completed the acquisition of Merus N.V. for USD 97.00 per share in cash, a transaction value of about USD 8.0 billion, accounted for as an asset acquisition because substantially all of the value is petosemtamab. The agreement was signed on 29 September 2025 and the tender offer began on 21 October 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition was funded with about USD 5.5 billion of new debt and cash on hand: a USD 1 billion Term Loan A, a USD 2 billion Term Loan B, a USD 500 million revolving credit facility, USD 1.5 billion of senior secured notes and USD 1.0 billion of senior unsecured notes, with Genmab Finance LLC named alongside Genmab A/S in the debt documents. At 30 September 2026 the four drawn instruments carried USD 926 million, USD 1,674 million, USD 1,439 million and USD 953 million, and the Term B margin had been cut from 3.00% to 2.00% in June 2026. Coupons, maturities, guarantors and collateral are not supplied, and management's target is gross leverage below 3x within two years of closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The governance and sponsor risk level is Medium. It is driven by a debt-funded acquisition and continued share purchases, because both draw on cash that could repay debt and raise the dependence on royalty cash flows, which implies higher refinancing pressure until leverage falls. Countervailing evidence is the repayment of USD 288 million of term loans, the lower Term B margin, the absence of dividends, of a sponsor and of related-party leakage, and an independent board.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genmab is an adequate but concentrated credit: one royalty stream carries USD 4,992 million of Merus acquisition debt, and it begins to erode in 2029, so creditors depend on deleveraging well before then. Net debt fell to USD 3,132 million at 30 September 2026 and nine-month EBITDA covered cash interest 4.53x, yet total debt is still 4.78x last-twelve-months operating profit, a proxy that sits below EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is a fourth-quarter and 2027 launch-spending step-up that outpaces royalty growth, because guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted operating profit between USD -43 million and USD 277 million against USD 452 million in the third quarter. The profile would be called stable only once gross leverage is on a path to the management target of below 3x by December 2027, which the nine-month repayment pace alone does not achieve.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C16; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6–7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue quality is high today but finite, because one product family generates most of it and its patents expire from 2029. Revenue was USD 3,238 million in nine months, up 21.64%, and DARZALEX royalties were USD 2,057 million, or 63.53% of revenue, up 17.95% on the prior year. Johnson & Johnson develops, sells and bears the costs of the product, so Genmab earns the royalty without selling or manufacturing cost, which is why it converts to cash and also why Genmab cannot steer it. US patent rights end in 2029, European rights in 2031 and Japanese rights begin to expire in 2030, and the annual filing expects royalties to fall materially from 2029, so the debt has to be paid down before the royalty base shrinks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the main financial constraint and cannot be stated on EBITDA, because 2025 depreciation and amortization are not supplied. Total debt of USD 4,992 million is 4.78x last-twelve-months operating profit of USD 1,044 million and net debt of USD 3,132 million is 3.00x; on the company's adjusted operating profit of USD 1,356 million the multiples are 3.68x and 2.31x. Management targets gross leverage below 3x within two years of the December 2025 closing. At the nine-month repayment pace of USD 288 million, debt would be about USD 4,512 million by the end of 2027, which is 3.33x adjusted profit and 4.32x reported profit at today's levels, so the target needs profit growth of 10.91% on the adjusted measure or 44.06% on reported profit, or faster repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C16; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-11-06_genmabinterimreportq32025.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is uneven, and the nine-month result is flattered by a low tax charge. Operating cash flow was USD 574 million against USD 885 million a year earlier, with only USD 3 million in the first quarter and USD 520 million in the third, because receivables, inventories, contract liabilities and other payables together absorbed USD 354 million. Taxes paid fell to USD 97 million from USD 317 million and the estimated tax rate dropped to 3.4%, which the company says is not indicative of future periods; at 18.9%, the prior-year rate, tax expense would have been USD 111.65 million higher over the nine months. Free cash flow of USD 555 million was 51.97% of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 28, 35; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-05-07_genmabinterimreportq12026.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt service is covered with room to spare today, but part of the room is being used for share purchases. Free cash flow, which is after interest, covered nine-month principal repayments of USD 288 million 1.93x and left USD 171 million once USD 96 million of share purchases were paid, and cash rose to USD 1,860 million. A buy-back that runs alongside repayment while leverage is above the management target is a financial-policy choice, and the restricted-payment limits that govern it sit in debt documents that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 44–45; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next year, but the refinancing profile cannot be placed. Cash of USD 1,860 million, all bank deposits, is 5.85x current borrowings of USD 318 million, which are the current portions of the Term A and Term B loans, and the notes have no current portion. A USD 500 million revolving facility was arranged in December 2025, but the borrowings note shows no revolver balance and its availability, maturity and conditions are not stated, and the annual filing also refers to an unsecured three-year revolving facility whose size is not stated. Maturity dates, coupons and covenant levels of the term loans and notes are not supplied; the company states that it complied with the Term A covenants at 30 September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; calculation C22; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 45–46; 20-F_2025-12-31_gmab-20251231_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 131

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The interest burden is manageable and market access looks open. Nine-month cash interest was USD 236 million, covered 4.53x by EBITDA of USD 1,068 million, and the implied cost of debt is about 6.65% on average borrowings. Four interest rate swaps of USD 406 million each, running to 30 June 2028, fix 62.46% of the term loans at carrying value and leave USD 976 million floating, so a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 9.76 million a year. The June 2026 cut in the Term B margin from 3.00% to 2.00% saves about USD 19 million a year on USD 1,900 million and suggests lenders accepted a lower spread six months after closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 45–47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are under pressure from launch preparation, and management's levers are real but costly. Revenue rose 21.64% but operating profit fell to USD 986 million from USD 1,007 million, an operating margin of 30.45% against 37.83%, because adjusted operating expenses rose 27.33% (research and development 24.09%, selling, general and administrative 35.65%) as petosemtamab and Rina-S trials and launch teams were funded, and acquisition and integration charges added USD 87 million. Capital expenditure was only USD 19 million, so flexibility sits in research, selling and administrative spend, and cutting it would weaken the pipeline that has to replace DARZALEX royalties.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C20; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 23–24, 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Guidance points to a heavy fourth quarter. Maintaining the 2026 range implies fourth-quarter adjusted operating expenses of USD 914 million to USD 1,054 million, 41.27% to 62.91% above USD 647 million in the third quarter, and adjusted operating profit between USD -43 million and USD 277 million against USD 452 million, so fourth-quarter operating cash flow would be expected to fall well below the third quarter's USD 520 million unless working capital reverses. Either the range is conservative or launch-related spending steps up sharply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 6–7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and market position, competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, access to refinancing, liquidity and financial policy are average, business diversification and free cash flow stability are weak, and none is strong. The weakest two follow from the same fact, a profit base that rests on one royalty and converts to cash unevenly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that the royalty base is still growing fast and the debt is being repaid from cash flow. DARZALEX royalties rose 17.95%, Kesimpta royalties rose to USD 408 million from USD 320 million, EPKINLY global net sales rose 47% to USD 491 million, net debt fell USD 427 million in nine months, the Term B margin was cut from 3.00% to 2.00%, and three Phase 3 trials read out positively in October 2026. The leverage proxies also overstate leverage, because operating profit is struck after depreciation and amortization of USD 82 million in nine months, which EBITDA adds back, and management's adjusted profit gives 3.68x gross, within reach of the target with moderate growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the debt documents show maturities beyond 2029, covenant headroom and tight restricted-payment limits, if fourth-quarter operating cash flow returns to the third-quarter level of USD 520 million, or if the launches of epcoritamab, Rina-S or petosemtamab add royalty-independent profit before 2029. It would worsen if growth in DARZALEX net sales falls below the 19% of nine months, if biosimilar or patent events reduce royalties before 2029, if first-quarter-style operating cash flow of USD 3 million recurs, if share purchases continue while leverage stays near today's 4.78x, or if the AbbVie or Chugai cases are decided against Genmab.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Royalty growth on a cost-free stream is the first support for creditors: royalties rose to USD 2,699 million from USD 2,219 million and are paid on partner sales, so each extra dollar of royalty reaches operating profit without Genmab selling cost, which raises debt service capacity while the patents last.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is comfortable: EBITDA of USD 1,068 million covered nine-month cash interest of USD 236 million 4.53x and free cash flow of USD 555 million covered principal repayments 1.93x, so the debt is serviced from operations and not from cash on hand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging has started and market access looks open: net debt fell USD 427 million to USD 3,132 million, USD 288 million of term loan principal was repaid and the Term B margin was cut to 2.00%, which lowers interest cost and signals lender appetite.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term liquidity is sound: cash of USD 1,860 million is 5.85x current borrowings and no note has a current portion, so scheduled repayment in the next twelve months is small against cash on hand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration is the dominant weakness: DARZALEX royalties are 63.53% of revenue and J&J is 66.99%, and US patents expire in 2029, so the cash flow that services the debt shrinks on a known date and the debt has to be reduced or refinanced against that decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high: total debt is 4.78x last-twelve-months operating profit against a management target of below 3x, so deleveraging has to come from repayment and profit growth together, and the cushion for a royalty shortfall is thin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is volatile: operating cash flow fell to USD 574 million from USD 885 million, with USD 3 million in the first quarter, and part of the nine-month result comes from a 3.4% tax rate that the company says will not recur, so debt service capacity in a weak quarter is lower than the nine-month average implies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Spending is rising faster than revenue: adjusted operating expenses grew 27.33% against revenue growth of 21.64%, and guidance implies a larger fourth quarter, so margin and cash conversion are exposed to launch timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor protections cannot be verified: the debt documents, agency views and the amounts of the AbbVie and Chugai claims are not supplied while share purchases continue, so the strength of covenants, restricted-payment limits and any legal loss cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The analysis runs as ready with limitations: four filings and three accepted analyses support a full synthesis, but the annual report, the credit agreement, the indentures, the first-half 2026 report and any agency view are missing, so EBITDA leverage, maturities and covenant headroom stay open. Entity, period and currency are consistent: the Genmab A/S group, US dollars, financial years to 31 December, and a latest period of nine months to 30 September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genmab is a Copenhagen antibody company whose credit rests on three streams: royalties on partner-sold medicines, net sales of its own products, and a late-stage pipeline. Royalties were USD 2,699 million, or 83.35% of nine-month revenue, and net product sales were USD 410 million, mostly EPKINLY in the US and Japan at USD 381 million. Royalty income is contractual and recurring and needs no Genmab funding of sales, but net product sales carry a profit share to AbbVie on EPKINLY of USD 184 million in nine months, so they add less cash for each dollar of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership adds no external support: Genmab is listed with no sponsor or parent, BlackRock and Orbis each hold 5.80%, management holds 1.27% and the board has a majority of independent directors. Creditors therefore rely on the borrower's own policy, which targets gross leverage below 3x, and on documents that are not supplied; no dividends have been paid and the credit agreement and indentures restrict distributions, yet share purchases of USD 96 million continued.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring, partner-controlled and finite. DARZALEX net sales by J&J were USD 12,410 million in nine months, up 19%, and the company guides 2026 DARZALEX royalties at about USD 2.83 billion at the midpoint. The royalty tiers run from 12% to 20% of annual net sales and are reduced country by country on patent expiry and on the first biosimilar sale, so pricing power and the pace of decline sit with J&J, not with Genmab. Kesimpta and TEPEZZA add diversification, and EPKINLY net sales grew 47% on demand in later-line lymphoma and second-line follicular lymphoma, but none of them yet offsets DARZALEX.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly discretionary research, selling and administrative spend, which was 58.55% of nine-month revenue against 55.94% a year earlier. The variable costs are the AbbVie profit share and royalty expense of USD 29 million, which grow with EPKINLY sales, and operating leverage is currently negative because launch preparation for Rina-S and petosemtamab and the Merus integration add cost before revenue. Foreign exchange was a net loss of USD 10 million in nine months, so currency is not a main driver of margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is minimal, so conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow depends on interest, tax and working capital. Capital expenditure was USD 19 million in nine months, while interest on borrowings took USD 229 million of cash, which did not exist a year earlier, taxes took USD 97 million, and working capital took USD 354 million as receivables from collaboration partners rose to USD 992 million from USD 907 million. Free cash flow of USD 555 million, 51.97% of EBITDA, therefore depends on partner collection timing and on a tax rate that is not durable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 47; calculation C7; calculation C17; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry and substitution are the main forces. DARZALEX competes in multiple myeloma with CAR-T therapies and bispecific antibodies, including J&J's own TECVAYLI and TALVEY, on which Genmab also earns royalties that were not material in nine months, so substitution inside the J&J portfolio offsets little; epcoritamab competes with Regeneron's odronextamab and Roche's mosunetuzumab and glofitamab. Because royalties fall country by country once a biosimilar is sold, biosimilar entry, not only patent expiry, can end the royalty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power and policy are the second force. Payers set coverage, the Inflation Reduction Act lets Medicare negotiate prices, DARZALEX was not among the first ten drugs negotiated, and most-favoured-nation targets apply to biologics without biosimilar competition; the effect on royalties is uncertain, but a lower net price lowers the royalty in proportion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier and partner power matter more than usual. J&J controls DARZALEX, AbbVie shares EPKINLY profits and is also litigating against Genmab over Rina-S, and the contract manufacturer for Rina-S is exposed to US action against Chinese biotechnology companies, which could delay a launch. New entrants matter little within the debt tenor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other macro factors are not a primary credit driver: tariffs and exchange rates are cited, but the net foreign exchange loss was USD 10 million in nine months, so political and economic factors matter through drug pricing and manufacturing only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The opportunities that could improve credit quality are the potential launches in 2027 of epcoritamab in earlier lines, Rina-S in ovarian cancer and petosemtamab in head and neck cancer, after positive topline results in October 2026. The threats are earlier royalty erosion, pricing regulation, the AbbVie and Chugai litigation and the integration of Merus, which was 59.6% of total assets at 31 December 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the outlook is positive for revenue and uncertain for cash. Guidance for 2026 is revenue of USD 4,325 million to USD 4,525 million, royalties of USD 3,625 million to USD 3,750 million and adjusted operating profit of USD 1,065 million to USD 1,385 million, which supports a further fall in leverage if the range holds; lower interest from the Term B repricing and from repaid debt is a tailwind, and launch spending is the headwind. Potential launches in 2027 would add cost before revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6–7; calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outlook is dominated by 2029. Royalties are expected to fall materially after US patent expiry, while the company gives no guidance beyond 2026, so whether EPKINLY, Rina-S and petosemtamab replace DARZALEX royalties of USD 2,057 million in nine months is not established. Sector headwinds are pricing regulation and biosimilars, and the company-specific headwind is carrying USD 8,237 million of in-process research and development acquired with Merus.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside that matters is a slowdown in DARZALEX royalties while launch spending is already committed. The initiating condition is growth in partner net sales slowing from 19% toward zero through competition from CAR-T therapies and bispecifics, price regulation or an early biosimilar. The first operational break is margin: royalties carry almost no cost, so each 10% fall in guided DARZALEX royalties of about USD 2.83 billion removes about USD 283 million of operating profit, which is 26.01% of the guided 2026 midpoint of USD 1,088 million, while spending for Rina-S and petosemtamab continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; calculation C18; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-11-05_genmabinterimreportq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission is leverage and cash: gross debt of USD 4,992 million would be 6.20x and net debt 3.89x the reduced profit of USD 805 million, and free cash flow, USD 555 million in nine months, would shrink toward principal repayments of USD 288 million. Liquidity holds for a year because cash of USD 1,860 million is 5.85x current borrowings, but refinancing capacity would then depend on pipeline value and lender appetite rather than on royalty growth. The levers are real, since research, selling and administrative spend of USD 1,896 million over nine months is discretionary and share purchases of USD 96 million can stop, but using them delays the launches that must replace DARZALEX royalties. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within a year and insufficient to meet the leverage target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C18; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A failure of petosemtamab would not move cash, yet in-process research and development of USD 8,237 million exceeds shareholders' equity of USD 6,333 million, so a full write-off would eliminate equity; whether any covenant tests equity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Genmab presents an adequate business profile supported by growing royalty income that carries no Genmab cost, interest cover of 4.53x and cash of USD 1,860 million, but credit quality is constrained by concentration in DARZALEX royalties, leverage of 4.78x last-twelve-months operating profit and unverified debt documents. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because operating cash flow fell to USD 574 million and guidance implies a heavy fourth quarter. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on debt maturities that are not supplied, on the lender appetite shown by the June 2026 margin cut and on launch success before 2029. The primary downside path is a DARZALEX royalty slowdown while launch spending is committed. Further analysis would require the Annual Report 2025, the credit agreement and indentures, the first-half 2026 report, agency views and peer data. Top risk: DARZALEX royalty erosion from 2029 before leverage has fallen below the management target.
